summary: Independent review of the consolidated Release Intelligence v2.0.0-GA GOLDEN BUILD ZIP SHA256 ebc3fc2b478e0bfda4efc0e30bd29b8a5528f0bead9354295b718f70799cdf77. All 27 packaged files byte-match source. It includes the reviewed usage notifications, executive action order, product/context headings, and latest alignment fixes. Multiselect labels use textContent and a decorative aria-hidden CSS caret; centered SVG expand/create icons retain accessible button names and existing delegated handlers. The unique GA asset cache suffix distinguishes this consolidated build. The archived original GA ZIP remains present with its previously reviewed SHA256 96ff7a49e2707682511017abbda6dabda6ef1e8370649061a63300415020b5fc. Independently executed all nine focused controls tests successfully. No blocking issues found. Overall application risk remains High under the existing rubric assessment.
caveats: The repeated v2.0.0-GA designation identifies this newly authorized consolidated baseline. Use its exact SHA256 and unique asset cache suffix to distinguish it from the archived original; GA/GOLDEN BUILD does not eliminate inherited operational risks.

Usage reflects metadata returned to this client for the explicit operation, not organization-wide consumption, billing, or all server-side model activity. Failed, cancelled, backend-only, or unreported calls can leave totals incomplete, as labeled.

Input totals include reported cache-read and cache-creation tokens in addition to input_tokens. This matches the inspected Anthropic-style usage contract; actual production SDK/model usage values were not verified.
Concurrent completed operations share one notification shell; the newest notice replaces the preceding one. Notices expire after five seconds and are not a durable usage ledger.

Existing model grounding, goal-versus-outcome, temporal-evidence, snapshot/cache/cancellation, popup accessibility/scroll, refresh concurrency, journal growth, revision conflict, non-atomic update, preference, host/catalog/history limit, and AllUsers sharing caveats remain.
Current GUS Apps host metadata still relies on verified-definition snapshots; automatic detection of future list-column changes remains unavailable without live list-view REST capability.

This review combined static source/artifact inspection with nine independently executed focused controls tests. The implementing agent reported all 138 Node tests and alignment, multiselect, compact-epic, usage, and method browser checks passed; those full suites and production-host/model behavior were not independently verified. Git tag movement, remote publication, and Pages deployment were outside this review.
